cohort: 29,124 patients undergoing Cesarean section and 9,767 patients undergoing hysterectomy
finding: Intravenous acetaminophen was associated with shorter length of stay, reduced opioid consumption, and lower risk of opioid-related adverse events compared to oral acetaminophen in patients undergoing Cesarean section or hysterectomy.
mod_finding: Post-surgical pain managed with intravenous acetaminophen in patients undergoing Cesarean section or hysterectomy was associated with shorter length of stay, reduced risk of opioid-related adverse events, and lower opioid consumption compared to patients managed with oral acetaminophen.
